rationale: RECEIVER OWNERSHIP (Lead contract, replacing the earlier `ownerType` proposal): the store resolves calls/uses rows through `metadata.owner` — src/ast/member-owner-resolution.ts `claimOwnerCarryingTargets` + `resolveMemberTargetsByOwner`, called from both resolution paths in src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts. It requires exactly one CLASS-LIKE owner (class|interface|trait|enum; a dart mixin/extension is not class-like to that rule), filters member candidates by kind, walks the owner's ancestors via brain_symbol.super_types, and WITHDRAWS the row's name binding when the owner cannot verify — which is why a WRONG owner is worse than none and why this fixture pins the two absences as hard as the four presences. The four evidence classes are the receiver contract's: `param` (signature parameter type), `field` (the symbol pass's fieldTypeByField), `annotation` (a local/for-in binding with a written type), `assignment` (a local whose type comes from its initializer construction). The emission is ADDITIVE: the target spelling is byte-identical to HEAD; only metadata is added. The `useExternal` case is the one that matters most for resolution — `HttpClient` is written in the signature but declared nowhere in this file, so the target is the spelled `HttpClient.close` carrying `baseBeyondRunScope`, and the owner channel is the half a store can act on when the in-file key space cannot.

expectSymbols.name: Coord
expectSymbols.note: a typedef is a published TYPE symbol — and NOT class-like to the owner rule

expectRelationships.note: EVIDENCE 1 — PARAM: `void useParam(Repo r) { r.load(); }`. The type is written in the signature; the owner channel states it and the evidence class says WHERE the answer came from. Target unchanged (Repo.load).
EVIDENCE 1 on the READ arm (`r.count`) — the same evidence covers calls and member reads; a request that only wired one arm would pass the calls pin and fail this one.

EVIDENCE 2 — FIELD: `Holder.repo` is declared `final Repo repo`, so a read of `repo.load()` inside Holder knows the receiver's type from the field's own declaration. The `run` source is the enclosing method's own name (only one `run` is annotated here).

EVIDENCE 3 — ANNOTATION: `final Repo r2 = Repo();` writes the type. Distinct from the assignment case below on purpose: the two are different evidence classes and a consumer must be able to tell a WRITTEN type from a CONSTRUCTED one.

EVIDENCE 4 — ASSIGNMENT: `final r3 = Repo();` names no type; the type comes from the initializer's construction. The owner is still EXACT (a construction names its class), but the evidence class says the source did not write the type.

THE RESOLUTION CASE — `HttpClient` is a parameter type declared NOWHERE in this fixture, so the in-file walk cuts the row to its spelled form with the `baseBeyondRunScope` claim. The owner channel is the piece a project resolver can act on: the type name is written in the source, so `owner` is exact even though the type's declaration is not in this run. Both halves are pinned — the claim AND the owner — because a fix that added the owner by dropping the claim would launder a spelling into an exemption.

TYPEDEF RECEIVER — `coord.x` where coord's type is the typedef `Coord`. The type IS statically known, but a typedef is not class-like to the store's resolver, so NO owner is emitted: an owner it cannot accept makes the resolver withdraw the row's binding. The cut (receiverMemberOutsideRun) is the honest state.

MIXIN RECEIVER — the call target still spells the mixin owner (`Loggy.logIt`) because visibleTypes includes the in-file mixin, but `metadata.owner` is absent for the same reason. The target spelling and the owner channel are different questions.

forbidRelationships.note: NO OWNER FOR `this` RECEIVERS: the target spelling already names the owner, and "the enclosing class" is not one of the four evidence classes. A fix that attached owner to every row with a determinate receiver would pass the four positive pins and fail here.

and not with a borrowed evidence class either — this is the same wrong row spelled differently, because the evidence class alone would be a claim about HOW a type was known that the source never says.

NO INFERENCE: `final x = makeThing(); x.go();` — the initializer is a CALL, not a construction, so nothing at the site names x's type. The `makeThing` return type is not read back through the call, and asserting `Object` would be the guess the contract forbids. The row keeps its bare leaf and its receiver cut.
and no evidence class without an owner — the pair travels together or not at all.

THE ALIAS IS NOT THE OWNER: `Repo` is the published type name; `r` is the value's name. The store looks the owner up as a class-like declaration, so a value name would make every owner-carrying row decline.
NO OWNER FOR A TYPEDEF — the resolver accepts only class|interface|trait|enum; a typedef owner would be declined AND withdraw the name binding.
NO OWNER FOR A MIXIN — same rule; a mixin is not class-like to member-owner-resolution.
